caption:
A slow order search needs a query-plan check before another index. Follow one orders workload from a table scan to an index, a customer/date filter and a covering query. Indexes also need storage and write maintenance.

In PostgreSQL, index-only scans can still visit the heap when visibility checks require it. Compare representative reads and writes with EXPLAIN before keeping an index. Useful for a teammate investigating a slow query.
#systemdesign #beyondlocalhost

takeaway: Inspect the actual query plan first
Measure representative reads and index maintenance

scenes.title: The search keeps looking
scenes.narration: Your order search checks row after row before it finds order forty-two in the table.
scenes.note: Illustrative table scan; no timing benchmark.

scenes.title: Follow the index entry
scenes.narration: A matching index gives this query another path: find the entry, then fetch the order record when the query needs its columns.
scenes.note: The planner chooses the actual access path.

scenes.title: Now filter this customer
scenes.narration: Our order screen also lists one customer’s recent orders. The query filters by customer and date, then sorts the matching orders by date.
scenes.note: Keep the same orders workload, not a new app.

scenes.title: Column order shapes the path
scenes.narration: A composite B-tree starting with customer and then date can support that pattern. Different filters and sorting can need a different index arrangement.
scenes.note: Leading equalities and the first range shape the scan.

scenes.title: Can the index answer alone?
scenes.narration: If the index stores every needed column, an index-only scan may avoid table visits. PostgreSQL still checks visibility and sometimes fetches the table.
scenes.note: Index-only scans depend on visibility, not just columns.

scenes.title: Writes maintain extra structure
scenes.narration: Changing an indexed value also means maintaining its index entry. Extra indexes take storage and can add work to writes, so measure both paths.
scenes.note: Update reaches the table and index; illustrative work path.

scenes.title: Check the query you run
scenes.narration: Use EXPLAIN to inspect the chosen query plan. Test representative reads and writes before keeping an index, and send the actual query with your findings.
scenes.note: Check a representative workload; avoid blanket index advice.
